cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State the index law a^m × a^n.
cards.back: a^(m+n), for the same non-zero base.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State the index law (a^m)^n.
cards.back: a^(mn).

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is logₐ1?
cards.back: 0, since a⁰ = 1 (a > 0, a ≠ 1).

cards.front: What is logₐa?
cards.back: 1, for a > 0 and a ≠ 1.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State the point–gradient form of a straight-line equation.
cards.back: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁).

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is the sum of n terms of an arithmetic progression?

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is the sum of n terms of a geometric progression?
cards.back: Sₙ = a(1−rⁿ)/(1−r), when r ≠ 1.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is the sum to infinity for a convergent geometric series?
cards.back: S∞ = a/(1−r), valid when |r| < 1.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is the radian sector-area formula?
cards.back: A = ½r²θ, with θ in radians.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State the identity linking sec²x and tan²x.
cards.back: sec²x = 1 + tan²x.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State the identity linking cosec²x and cot²x.
cards.back: cosec²x = 1 + cot²x.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is sin 2x in terms of sin x and cos x?
cards.back: sin 2x = 2 sin x cos x.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is cos 2x in terms of cos²x and sin²x?
cards.back: cos 2x = cos²x − sin²x.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is tan 2x in terms of tan x?
cards.back: tan 2x = 2 tan x/(1−tan²x), where defined.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is d(sin kx)/dx?
cards.back: k cos(kx), using radians.

cards.front: What is d(cos kx)/dx?
cards.back: −k sin(kx), using radians.

cards.back: 1/x (for x > 0).

cards.front: State the product rule for y = uv.
cards.back: dy/dx = u′v + uv′.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State the quotient rule for y = u/v.
cards.back: dy/dx = (vu′ − uv′)/v².

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State the chain rule for y = f(g(x)).
cards.back: dy/dx = f′(g(x))g′(x).

cards.front: What is ∫e^(kx) dx, for k ≠ 0?
cards.back: e^(kx)/k + C.

cards.back: −cos(kx)/k + C.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: State integration by parts in its standard form.
cards.back: ∫u(dv/dx) dx = uv − ∫v(du/dx) dx.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: How is a value standardised for X ~ N(μ,σ²)?
cards.back: z = (x−μ)/σ.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: For X~B(n,p), what are E(X) and Var(X)?
cards.back: E(X) = np; Var(X) = np(1−p).

For y = f(ax), what happens to x-coordinates?

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is a one-sided hypothesis test looking for?
cards.back: Evidence of a difference in one specified direction.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: In variable-acceleration motion, how is v related to displacement s?
cards.back: v = ds/dt.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: In variable-acceleration motion, how is a related to v?
cards.back: a = dv/dt.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For a product or quotient, how do percentage uncertainties combine?
cards.back: Add percentage uncertainties (usual worst-case estimate).

similarCandidates.front: How are percentage uncertainties combined for a product of measured quantities?

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How can uncertainty in a fitted line's y-intercept be estimated?
cards.back: Compare best-fit with extreme acceptable line intercepts.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What two conservation laws must hold in pair production?
cards.back: Energy and momentum are both conserved.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why can't a single photon create a pair in empty space?
cards.back: A lone photon cannot conserve both energy and momentum.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the strangeness of an s quark?
cards.back: −1 (an anti-s has +1).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the distinction between amplitude and peak-to-peak displacement?
cards.back: Peak-to-peak displacement is twice the amplitude.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: When are two superposed waves exactly in antiphase?
cards.back: They have a phase difference of 180° or π radians.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For a Hooke's-law spring, how is stored strain energy found?
cards.back: E = ½Fx = ½kx², from the force–extension graph area.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What defines the critical temperature of a superconductor?
cards.back: At or below it the material's resistivity is zero.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What changes in an emf–terminal-voltage graph as current rises?
cards.back: Lost volts Ir increases; terminal p.d. decreases.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the acceleration at the equilibrium position in SHM?
cards.back: Zero, because displacement x = 0.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: In the gas equation pV = NkT, what does N count?
cards.back: The number of gas molecules, not moles.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why is rms speed not the same as mean speed?
cards.back: Rms uses the square root of the mean squared speed.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does an equipotential surface tell you about work along it?
cards.back: No work is done by the electric field moving charge along it.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why does the unit of molar concentration change when volume uses cm³?
cards.back: Concentration uses dm³, so convert cm³ to dm³ first.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the difference between a bond pair and a lone pair?
cards.back: A bond pair is shared between atoms; a lone pair is not.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: In calorimetry, why may the calculated |ΔH| be too small?
cards.back: Heat loss to surroundings makes measured |ΔT| too small.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What happens to Kc if concentrations change but temperature stays constant?
cards.back: It stays the same; the position may shift.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why do we weigh both benefits and risks of water chlorination?
cards.back: It prevents infections, but toxic chlorine or by-products require control.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the role of the nucleophile in nucleophilic substitution?
cards.back: It donates an electron pair to the electrophilic carbon.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What distinguishes an addition polymer from its monomer?
cards.back: The monomer's C=C bonds open to form a saturated chain.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What distinguishes oxidation of primary and secondary alcohols?
cards.back: Primary can form aldehyde/acid; secondary forms ketone.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What does a positive 2,4-DNPH test usually indicate?
cards.back: An aldehyde or ketone carbonyl group.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is ΔG in terms of ΔH and ΔS?
cards.back: ΔG = ΔH − TΔS, with consistent units.

similarCandidates.front: What is oxidation in terms of electrons and oxidation state?
What is reduction in terms of electrons and oxidation state?

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What quantity, not concentration, is used in a Kp expression?
cards.back: Equilibrium partial pressure of each gas.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What is the pKa definition?
cards.back: pKa = −log₁₀(Ka).

similarCandidates.front: What does 'standard state' mean in enthalpy definitions?
What is the definition of Hess's law?

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How is [H⁺] found from a pH value?
cards.back: [H⁺] = 10^(−pH) mol dm⁻³.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How does an acidic buffer resist small pH changes?
cards.back: HA removes added OH⁻; A⁻ removes added H⁺.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why do transition-metal complex ions often have colour?
cards.back: Ligand-field splitting allows absorption of visible wavelengths.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What does a zero discriminant tell you about a quadratic?
cards.back: It has one repeated real root.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: How is the domain of f⁻¹ related to f?
cards.back: It is the range of f.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: How is the range of f⁻¹ related to f?
cards.back: It is the domain of f.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What does a remainder of zero show about a polynomial divisor (x−a)?
cards.back: (x−a) is a factor of the polynomial.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What does Σ from r=1 to n mean?
cards.back: Add the listed expression for r = 1, 2, …, n.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: For a geometric sum, what happens when r=1?
cards.back: All n terms equal a, so Sₙ = na.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What are the exact values of sin(π/6) and cos(π/3)?
cards.back: Both equal 1/2.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What are the exact values of sin(π/4) and cos(π/4)?
cards.back: Both equal √2/2.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What does f′(a)=0 tell you about a smooth curve?
cards.back: It has a stationary point at x=a.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: Why is the constant of integration needed in an indefinite integral?
cards.back: All antiderivatives differ by a constant.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What operation replaces dx when using integration by substitution?
cards.back: Replace the integrand and differential consistently in the new variable.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: When does a sign change bracket a root?
cards.back: If f is continuous and f(a)f(b)<0, at least one root lies between.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What is the difference between a test statistic and a p-value?
cards.back: Statistic summarises data; p-value measures extremeness under H₀.

cards.subject: Maths
cards.front: What conditions establish equilibrium of a rigid body in a plane?
cards.back: Resultant force zero and resultant moment zero.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is resolution of a digital measuring instrument?
cards.back: The smallest displayed change in the reading.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What must happen to both momentum and energy in annihilation?
cards.back: Both must be conserved.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What distinguishes strong from weak interactions in a strangeness-changing decay?
cards.back: Strangeness can change in weak interactions, not strong interactions.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why can below-threshold light not eject electrons by increasing intensity?
cards.back: Each photon has insufficient energy to overcome the work function.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: How much is one complete oscillation in radians of phase?
cards.back: 2π radians.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does a phase difference of π/2 represent?
cards.back: One-quarter of a cycle (90°).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: In double-slit interference, what is the path difference at the centre?
cards.back: Zero.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What does a negative velocity mean on a signed motion graph?
cards.back: Motion in the negative chosen direction.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why can displacement be zero when distance travelled is not?
cards.back: Opposite-direction displacements can cancel.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why does a filament lamp show increasing resistance as voltage rises?
cards.back: The filament gets hotter and its resistance rises.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Why does a diode have negligible reverse current normally?
cards.back: It strongly resists conduction under reverse bias.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the phase difference between SHM displacement and acceleration?
cards.back: π radians (180°), since a = −ω²x.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: For a monatomic ideal gas, how is U related to T?
cards.back: U = 3/2 nRT.

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: Which way does the induced current act relative to a flux change?
cards.back: It opposes the change that produced it (Lenz's law).

cards.subject: Physics
cards.front: What is the shape of a graph of ln(activity) against time?
cards.back: A straight line with gradient −λ.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: In a back titration, what does the measured leftover reagent determine?
cards.back: How much excess reagent remained after the first reaction.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How does an extra lone pair typically affect the bond angle?
cards.back: It reduces the bond angle through stronger repulsion.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Which feature of a Maxwell–Boltzmann curve gives the fraction above Eₐ?
cards.back: The area under the curve to the right of Eₐ.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: For an exothermic equilibrium, how does increasing T affect Kc?
cards.back: Kc decreases.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is barium sulfate suitable as an insoluble contrast compound?
cards.back: It is very insoluble, limiting release of barium ions.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Where must a full curly arrow start in an organic mechanism?
cards.back: At a lone pair or covalent bond containing the moving electron pair.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What type of reaction converts an alkene into an alkane?
cards.back: Addition of hydrogen (hydrogenation).

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why must an aldehyde be distilled off during primary-alcohol oxidation?
cards.back: To limit further oxidation to a carboxylic acid.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: When can an endothermic reaction be feasible from ΔG?
cards.back: When TΔS exceeds ΔH, making ΔG < 0.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What happens to rate if [A] doubles in a first-order reaction?
cards.back: Rate doubles, with other factors unchanged.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: What happens to rate if [A] doubles in a second-order reaction?
cards.back: Rate becomes four times larger, all else constant.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: When pressure changes at constant temperature, does Kp change?
cards.back: No; Kp depends only on temperature.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: How does a pH meter differ from an indicator at equivalence?
cards.back: It measures the full pH change rather than only a colour transition.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why can two complexes of the same metal ion have different colours?
cards.back: Different ligands change d-orbital splitting and absorbed wavelengths.

cards.subject: Chemistry
cards.front: Why is TMS a useful chemical-shift reference?
cards.back: It produces a single signal defined as δ = 0 ppm.
